A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffSampling research. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and full appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original decoding experiments on GSM8K, MATH, XSum, and DAT, including appendix sensitivity analyses and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds WritingPrompts experiments, stricter DAT evaluation, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains distribution sorting, largest-gap truncation, the lower-bound and min-p relaxations, and temperature scaling after truncation. Different experimental parameter choices do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds open-ended story generation on WritingPrompts, extending evaluation beyond v2's mathematical solutions, short summaries, and noun lists to longer narratives. GSM8K, MATH, MetaMathQA, XSum, and DAT coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Contrastive search is removed from the math, XSum, DAT, and appendix MetaMathQA comparisons where it participated in v2. Greedy decoding, top-p, min-p, eta-sampling, and locally typical sampling remain; newly cited logit-space sampling is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Primary settings change from p_lb=0.8 to 0.9 and p_min=0.3 to 0.1 to match the corresponding baselines. WritingPrompts introduces 500 test prompts, five outputs per prompt, 1,024-token generation, Llama-3.2-3B models, and per-input diversity evaluation. An additional DAT protocol requires and scores all ten distinct nouns, while retaining the seven-noun main evaluation.

E4.justification: v3 adds the ten-noun DAT robustness check in Figure 5 and extends temperature, truncation-order, and parameter-sensitivity analyses to story generation. Existing sweeps gain p_lb=0.95 and p_min=0.05 settings. Qualitative evidence is also revised, including replaced math/XSum examples and new story repetition analyses.

E5.justification: v3 newly identifies seeds 1, 42, and 121 and the seed-setting function. Three-seed evaluations, 100 DAT generations, standard errors, and 95% confidence intervals already appear in v2; no increased run count is established for retained experiments. The new story task also documents repeated generation.

E6.justification: v3 adds WritingPrompts results, ten-noun DAT findings, and additional threshold results, such as GSM8K accuracy 64.82±0.31 at p_lb=0.95 in Table 15. Relaxed-variant temperature/order results and qualitative outputs are replaced under changed defaults. Several revised main-table values already appeared in v2's ablation tables, so their relocation is not a new same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the sorted-distribution setup, and the heuristic argument that the largest gap occurs at or before the true-distribution boundary are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: v3 qualifies the abstract and conclusion: broad quality-and-diversity competitiveness becomes quality parity with the methods being extended, with potential diversity improvements. The central derivative-based truncation contribution remains, with additional emphasis on longer generation.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the relaxed variants more explicitly as near-baseline corrections and adds explanations of story diversity and persistent DiffSampling-cut repetition. It removes v2's substantive limitations concerning learned grammatical biases, unchanged stored knowledge, and inability to reduce memorization, retaining a shorter discussion of small models and automatic evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 adds precise model identifiers, Linux/Python 3.11.9 information, seed-setting instructions, baseline-parameter selection rationale, and story prompts. Reported hardware changes from two L40 GPUs plus one H100 to two 80GB H100 GPUs. Conversely, v2's code-availability link is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tang et al. on logit-space sampling, Fu et al. on repetition, and Chung et al. for creative-writing prompts, while removing the Franceschelli et al. compression/copyright citation. The existing desmoothing positioning remains, with greater emphasis on correcting established decoding strategies.

P1.justification: The revision substantially reorganizes the document: numbered sections and lettered appendices become unnumbered, limitations are abridged into Discussion, and qualitative DAT discussion moves ahead of math and summarization. Results, discussion, and conclusion passages are extensively revised, and appendix prose is gathered before most displays.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, v2's separate DAT figures are combined, and the temperature overview changes from separate method panels to overlaid comparison curves. New tables and the ten-noun DAT figure accompany extensive display relocation, changed page formatting, and bold annotations marking the first divergent tokens in qualitative examples.

improvement.justification: WritingPrompts addresses v2's acknowledged lack of longer-form testing, and the ten-noun DAT check tests full compliance with the prompt. Matched default comparisons and more qualified claims make the evidence easier to interpret. These benefits outweigh, but are tempered by, removal of the code link and substantive caveats, plus new reporting inconsistencies: instructed-greedy WritingPrompts EAD is 0.17 in Table 4 but 0.06 in Table 8.
